dimensions.note: No settings, no vault fields, no secrets in schemas or logs. GitHub reads use the environment's existing gh sign-in; the extension stores and logs no token. Only GET `gh api` calls, so a read-only token is enough.

run logs info on entry ('Checking {repository} on {where}') and on completion ('{answer}') with structured props; a failed SPDX lookup or missing git is a warning. Confirmed with live workflow runs that swamp's logger prints both lines. Nothing sensitive is logged.

Every failure throws before writeResource. A bad repo string, a missing path, an unknown GitHub repository and a non-404 gh failure each throw with the repo/path and gh's stderr. 404 is told apart from other failures, and an empty repository is a no, not an error. SPDX lookup failures in the local path are caught narrowly and logged. Minor: a path that is a file, not a directory, fails with the raw 'Not a directory (os error 20): lstat .../README.md/.git' (seen live). It is still a failure, but the message could be clearer.

38 tests pass under make test. They cover every AC, the error paths (bad repo, missing path, unknown repo, gh auth failure, failed SPDX lookup, git missing), the gh/git subprocess reads through a faked Deno.Command, the execute wiring and both workflows. They use their own io/Command fakes, not createModelTestContext, which is enough for a method with one write. deno lint finds one unused import (GlobalArgsSchema) in the test file.

Read-only: no create or delete. Each run writes a new version of the single 'result' resource, and an interrupted run leaves nothing partial because the write is the last step. git status was unchanged after six live runs.

GitHub responses are shape-checked: the contents listing must be an array and entries are filtered by type=='file' and string name; the licence body is read through optional chaining, and NOASSERTION is mapped to null. 404 is detected from gh's body and stderr. Endpoints repos/{o}/{r}/contents/, /license and repos/{o}/{r} match the GitHub REST docs. The contents API caps a directory listing at 1000 entries, so a root with more entries could miss a licence. No pagination or rate-limit handling, which is acceptable for 1 to 3 calls per run.

No handles are left open: Deno.Command(...).output() collects and ends each subprocess, and readDir is iterated to the end. Tests remove their temp dirs in finally. No cloud resources are created. gh has no timeout of its own, but the workflow's maxWallClock of 30m bounds it.

Published files are README.md, LICENSE, the model and two workflows. They contain no IPs, internal hostnames, emails or account IDs. Fixtures use acme/tool, and the only real repository named is the public one in the spec (puddle-works/swamp-for-everything). The local request URL is not in the README. The README line 'A local check needs git on the PATH' is out of date: only the SPDX lookup needs git now.

All schemas are plain z.object with no passthrough. checked is an enum and the nullable fields are explicit. ResultSchema {args, items, ranAt} matches the written object field for field, and every LicenceSchema field is set on every path (mechanical checks 1 and 4 pass; there is no pagination cap to report, so check 2 does not apply).
The single resource spec 'result' has lifetime infinite and garbageCollection 20, which suits a small per-run answer record.
Not a CRUD lifecycle behaviour: a single read-only check method with nothing to create, update or delete.
No mutating methods: run only reads the filesystem, git and gh api GETs.
One method writes one instance named 'result' to the one spec, so nothing can collide (mechanical check 3).
Nothing is read back from stored state; there are no update, delete or sync methods.
Initial version 2026.10.30.1 with an empty globalArguments schema; model.version matches manifest.yaml, and no earlier version needs an upgrade.
